prompt:
Generate a REVISED DAYTIME concept for the user's extreme roller coaster in a stylized faceted coastal 3D game. Three local images are supplied: image 1 is ONLY the world's material/style and coastline reference, its tame hills MUST BE REPLACED; image 2 is real Takabisha structural inspiration for the BEYOND-VERTICAL drop; image 3 is real Full Throttle structural inspiration for a complete VERTICAL LOOP, with an upside-down train inside its top. Do NOT reproduce photo textures, brand names, signs or watermarks.
The user rejected image 1 because it looks like gentle hills and bigger architecture, not a frightening ride. The new track itself must dominate the image with clearly identifiable UPSIDE-DOWN elements. Main composition, wide 16:9 landscape, low oblique overview from the entrance, showing full sky silhouettes and entire loops down to their bases. Foreground station/buildings only 15 percent of image, ride steelwork 75 percent. Keep the existing faceted world, blue-gray steel, gray-white concrete, restrained cyan track accents, amber details, teal coastal water, small white-helmet avatar proportions.
Mandatory visible track silhouette:
- Far left a slender 85-metre lift tower with almost vertical ascent, crest and a visibly INWARD CURLING 110-degree drop plunging into a rock trench. The top is markedly higher than every other element. The drop must be visibly past vertical, like the Takabisha photo, not a diagonal ramp.
- Center foreground/midground an enormous complete 50-metre VERTICAL TEARDROP LOOP, an unmistakable upright ring with a large open sky hole. Riders traverse up its near side, UPSIDE DOWN under its top, and back down. The paired rails and triangular track spine twist continuously through it. One orange train is clearly upside down inside the top of this loop, tiny compared with the loop. Exactly one train in the whole image.
- To the right a SECOND separate complete 35-metre tilted vertical loop with another clearly visible open sky hole. Offset it spatially so both loop holes and complete outlines remain legible. These two loops are the focal point, NOT inverted-U hills, arches, or banked horizontal circles. Both tracks MUST close around the sky holes, with entry/exit runouts at the bases.
- Behind/between them a compact cobra-roll element, two twisting half loops joined at the top, showing a different rollover silhouette.
- Lower right by the cliff a clear DOUBLE CORKSCREW, the track making two rotations around its forward travel axis like a helix, with open centers.
- A short inverted horizontal stall over a rock chasm and a low barrel-roll return above the water provide lower layers. These are linked in one continuous ride, with substantial vertical clearance at crossovers, no junctions, no floating ends.
Scary engineering silhouette: a huge vertical drop and a cluster of genuinely upside-down track elements; do not use decorative rings that are detached from the ride. Build credible braced steel supports and small concrete footings only where necessary. Maintain irregular coastal peninsula with rock coves, small patches of grass and trees. Scene stays within a playable game world, no fantasy city, no giant decorative buildings. Crisp neutral daylight reveals the track and all inversion openings. No UI, no captions, no lettering, no diagram arrows, no photographic sky. This is an extreme ride-design concept, not a resort advertising picture.
